# Code of Conduct

This is a small project. The rules are simple.

## What we expect

- **Engage with substance, not personality.** Argue about the code, the design, or the decisions — not about the person making them.
- **Assume good faith.** Most disagreements come from missing context, not from bad intent. Ask questions before reacting.
- **Disagreement is welcome; rudeness is not.** Strong opinions, weakly held, expressed respectfully.
- **No discrimination, harassment, or hostility** based on any characteristic — gender, race, sexuality, nationality, disability, age, religion, technical experience level, or anything else. This isn't negotiable.

## What we don't expect

- That you agree with every framework decision. Open an issue, propose an ADR, or fork.
- That you sugarcoat technical critique. Be direct about what's wrong; be kind about how you say it.
- That you participate at all. Lurking is fine.

## If something goes wrong

If you experience or witness behavior that violates these expectations, email the maintainer privately at the address shown in the [git commit log](https://github.com/lloydbrian/lloydbriantech-ascent/commits/main). Reports will be handled discreetly.

The maintainer reserves the right to remove comments, close issues, ban contributors, or take other action proportional to the violation. This is a benevolent-dictatorship model while the project is small.

## Scope

This code applies in all project spaces: issues, pull requests, discussions, code comments, and any other communication that takes place in the context of the project.
